subject: Per-token breakpoints and streaming edge-cases
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <m.lopez@atlasai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: sales_ops@atlasai.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify how commit tiers apply for streaming spikes

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the latency profiles look promising. Before we move to procurement, legal asked us to get a little more detail on how Redwood will meter and bill streaming-based usage under a committed tier. A few specific questions from our finance/engineering teams: 

- Breakpoints: if we commit to a monthly token volume (e.g., 500M tokens) with tiered per-token pricing, how are the discount breakpoints evaluated? Is it based on daily aggregation, a true monthly aggregate, or per-request rounding?
- Streaming tokens: for streaming responses where partial tokens are emitted progressively, do you bill every emitted token immediately, or is there any client-side rounding/windowing that Redwood applies? We have long-running streams where tokens accumulate over time; we want to ensure spikes during a streamed session don’t push us into a higher price band unexpectedly or cause rounding to overshoot.
- Rounding rules: do you round up tokens per-response, per-stream-session, per-minute, or only at the billing snapshot? If rounding is applied per-request, that could materially change economics for us.

We'd like a brief write-up we can include in the SOW/contract appendix. If you have standard contract language for 'billable tokens' and 'streaming rounding', please share.

Can we get this by end of day Thursday (time-box for our legal review)?

Best,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Platform Partnerships, AtlasAI

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <m.lopez@atlasai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify how commit tiers apply for streaming spikes

Marta —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can paste to your SOW appendix; I also attached an updated pricing matrix and a short spec on streaming rounding. High level summary: 

1) Breakpoints and aggregation
- Discount breakpoints are evaluated against the calendar billing period aggregate for the account (monthly). We do not tier on a per-request or per-day basis. Final tier applied is based on total billable tokens consumed during the billing period.

2) Streaming token treatment
- Billable tokens are counted when the token is generated by the model (i.e., emitted in the stream).
- To reduce small-request inefficiencies, we apply a per-connection micro-window that aggregates tokens emitted within a 250ms window for rounding purposes only (this is not a monetary credit — it's a metering smoothing mechanism to reduce churn from micro-bursts).

3) Rounding and metering window
- We round down fractional token units inside the 250ms micro-window, and accumulate fractional remainders to the billing snapshot. At the billing snapshot (end of billing period), we apply standard half-up rounding on totals.
- Practically: per-token usage is deterministic at the millisecond level; the micro-window only affects how small bursts look on our metering streams and prevents per-request rounding noise.

4) Safeguards for commit tiers
- We include a usage-smoothing clause: if a single stream/session causes an anomalous spike (>= 2x typical 95th percentile minutes for 3 consecutive billing cycles), we will: (a) surface the event in the console, (b) allow a one-time review jointly with the customer, and (c) offer a one-time adjustment if we determine metering artifacts caused the spike.

Attached: pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx (matrix with per-tier breakpoints and effective per-token pricing), streaming-rounding-spec.md (2-page spec with examples).

If this looks ok, Rishi and Laura will help convert into contract language and a short appendix you can insert into the SOW. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk your legal through it.

Next steps (suggested):
- Marta confirm OK to proceed with the proposed micro-window approach (or highlight objectionable points).
- Redwood to provide a 1-paragraph SOW appendix and a short contract clause (we'll draft).

Thanks — talk soon.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0173

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marta Lopez <m.lopez@atlasai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify how commit tiers apply for streaming spikes

Marta/Team —

Adding a couple bookkeeping notes from billing/finance perspective so the SOW language is precise: 

- "Billable tokens" definition: billable token = number of model tokens emitted + tokens consumed in request context (i.e., prompt + user tokens), measured in whole-token units. Fractional tokens are aggregated and rounded at billing snapshot as Stephanie noted.
- Example: if your application emits 1,234.6 tokens in a billing window and consumes 765.3 prompt tokens, we aggregate to 1999.9 -> standard half-up rounding at month-end -> 2000 billable tokens.
- Micro-window effect: the 250ms micro-window is only applied to streaming emission smoothing and does not change how prompt tokens are counted. It reduces per-request rounding noise and is not a reliability adjustment.
- Invoice presentation: invoices show (a) gross token total, (b) applied committed volume, (c) overage tokens at on-demand rate, (d) effective blended rate after discount.

We'll draft contract text like: 
"Billable Tokens: Tokens generated by or submitted to the Model are counted as 'Billable Tokens'. Tokens are measured in whole-token units. Partial-token fractions will be summed for the billing period and rounded to the nearest whole token using standard half-up rounding. For streaming responses, Redwood applies a transient 250ms aggregation window for metering smoothing purposes only; such windowing shall not be applied as a discount or credit mechanism except as part of the anomaly review process defined below."

If you want, Rishi can turn the language into SOW-ready wording and we can attach to the pricing sheet.

-Laura

Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Billing & Revenue Systems
Redwood Inference

From: Marta Lopez <m.lopez@atlasai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, sales_ops@atlasai.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify how commit tiers apply for streaming spikes

Stephanie/Laura/Rishi —

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick confirmations from our legal/finance after reading your notes: 

1) The 250ms aggregation window is acceptable as long as the rounding/aggregation behavior is included in the SOW appendix and the anomaly review clause is available for exceptional spikes.
2) We request one additional clause: for any billing period where total billable tokens exceed the committed volume by more than 15% solely due to streaming aggregation artifacts (and not driven by end-customer load growth), Redwood will apply a one-time pro-rated credit equal to the overage amount above 15% after joint review.

If you can accept that addition, we can finalize the SOW appendix and route for signatures — we've allocated the procurement window for next week. I've reviewed the pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx and will mark the expected tier.

If you prefer, I'll sign the DocuSign when you send the final SOW appendix (link preferred).

Best,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Platform Partnerships, AtlasAI
